extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual read-speech corpus for speech research, derived from LibriVox audiobooks. It includes 8 languages and provides language models and baseline ASR models.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was prepared by downloading LibriVox audiobooks for selected languages using LibriVox APIs and data preparation tools from the Libri-Light open source library, then downsampling the audio and segmenting it into shorter utterances using trained acoustic models and streaming inference.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks in English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, and Polish; audio files from publicly shared user videos were also used to train the segmentation models.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: trained acoustic models in each of the languages using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss; wav2letter@anywhere framework
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is heavily dominated by English, with much smaller amounts of data in the other languages; it is also based on read speech from public-domain audiobooks, which may bias it toward audiobook narration style rather than spontaneous speech.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to read-speech audiobook data and may not generalize well to other speech styles; audio is downsampled to 16kHz and segmented into 10-20 second utterances for ASR training. The paper also notes that some benchmarks in other languages are low-scale or scattered, motivating MLS, but does not recommend specific non-uses.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support multilingual ASR research by providing a large open benchmark for languages beyond English, potentially improving access to speech technology across languages.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No explicit sensitive human attributes are described as being collected; the paper only mentions audio from publicly shared videos being de-identified, and the dataset itself is based on audiobook speech in multiple languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for automatic speech recognition research, including training acoustic models and language models, and for creating train, development, and test splits as well as limited-supervision training sets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz for further processing.
